title: Product Space Explorer
description: Pick a starting export basket and see how many products relatedness puts within one step's reach.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Knowledge Systems and Economic Complexity

educational.learningObjective: Given a simplified product space network, the learner will analyze which unexported products are most reachable from a country's current export basket by tracing relatedness edges, and justify why one candidate product is a better diversification target than another.
prerequisites: Has seen a network diagram with clusters
learningOutcomes: Identify which products are reachable from a given export basket
Justify one diversification target over another using relatedness
Explain why a sparse neighborhood limits future options regardless of current revenue
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a basket and ask for a ranked list of the two best diversification targets, with the shared capability named for each.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Preset selection plus one-step adjacency highlighting
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Contrasting starting conditions with an identical rule applied to both
pedagogical.feedbackType: Color-coded reachability plus a generated comparison between the two baskets
misconceptionsAddressed: That a country's next industry can be chosen freely
That current export value predicts future diversification options
discussionQuestions: Why does an oil-rich country stay undiversified despite enormous revenue?
Should industrial policy target the nearest product or the most valuable one?
Does the same logic apply to a company's product line, or to a person's career?
